newsitem.title: TURKEY: Mitsubishi unit in $1.5 bid for Turkish utility plant.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi unit in $1.5 bid for Turkish utility plant.

text.p: A consortium led by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd presented the lowest bid for Turkey's 1,400 MegaWatt coal-fired power plant tender, with a $1.51 billion offer, Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan said Wednesday.
He said the consortium included Babcock Lentjes of the United States, Mitsubishi Corp., Turkey's Gama, Tekfen, Tokar and Enka.

Kutan said authorities would take about five months to assess the bids, adding that the lowest price would not be the only criterion. "We will also look at how they will filter the chimneys against sulphur and other waste gases," he said.
According to the tender terms, the winner should build a gas filter with a 99-percent efficiency and desulphurizer with a 95-percent efficiency.
"Another thing we will look to is the proportion of Turkish companies in the consortia. The Mitsubishi consortium has the highest Turkish company contribution with 27 percent," Kutan said.

The Afsin-Elbistan B power plant, which will have four units each of 350 MW capacity, will exploit lignite coal in the Elbistan area, which has almost half of Turkey's total lignite reserves of 8.2 billion tons. It will produce about eight billion kiloWatt-hours annually, against a national power shortfall of about 2.5 billion kWh for 1997.
Turkey has been importing electricity from Iran, Georgia and Bulgaria since late 1996.
